- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.3) and forecast is below recent lows, increase forecast slightly to avoid underestimating rebound potential.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent peak), apply a 3–5 day lag correction: reduce forecast by 2–4% per day to reflect market cooling.  
- If forecast mean is consistently 2–3% above true outcome over 30d, apply a downward bias correction of 1–2% to the next 30d forecast.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.5–0.75 alternating), model should not overreact to single-day sentiment shifts — use 3-day moving average sentiment to smooth forecast adjustments.  
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows mean reversion to 65–70 range after 10–15d, reduce forecast slope toward that zone — avoid extrapolating beyond 10% deviation from recent 5d average.
